raw_text:
Great — here's a 12-week, progressive couch-to-5K plan tailored for a 24-year-old male with exercise-induced asthma (EIA), well controlled on a SABA. The program emphasizes gradual aerobic build, structured warm-ups, avoidance of uncontrolled high-intensity work in cold air, and practical asthma precautions. Follow medical advice and stop/examine symptoms if severe wheeze, chest tightness, lightheadedness, or significant breathlessness occur.

Overview and key safety notes
- Primary goal: complete a continuous 5K by the end of 12 weeks.
- Warm-up & cool-down: essential each session to reduce EIA risk. Warm-up = dynamic, progressive, 8–12 minutes; cool-down = 5–10 minutes easy walking + light stretching.
- Inhaler use: use SABA (short-acting β2 agonist) 10–15 minutes before exercise if your GP or asthma plan advises. Carry it on each run.
- Cold-air caution: avoid very cold, dry days or change sessions to a treadmill/indoor track. If training outdoors in cold, wear a scarf/buff over mouth and nose to warm/humidify inhaled air.
- Symptom action: if you experience wheeze, marked cough, chest tightness, or breathlessness unrelieved by inhaler, stop, use SABA, follow asthma action plan, seek medical help if no improvement.
- Frequency: 3 sessions per week on non-consecutive days (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri or Tue/Thu/Sat). Optional light cross-training (cycling, elliptical, swimming) on 1–2 other days once baseline fitness allows—keep intensity easy-moderate and asthma-safe.
- Progression: gradual increases in run time and reduced walk breaks. One week of easier load after every 3 weeks is built into plan via stepback or slightly reduced volume if needed.
- Strength/maintenance: two short strength sessions per week (15–20 minutes) focusing on glutes, core, and single-leg strength to support running form and reduce injury risk. These can be on non-run days or after easy runs.
- Recovery & sleep: aim for 7–9 hours sleep, hydrate, and prioritize easy nutrition (carbs + protein) within 60–90 minutes post-session.

Warm-up template (8–12 min)
- 3–5 min easy walk → brisk walk → easy jog for last 1–2 min (as able).
- Add dynamic drills: leg swings (front/back, 8–10 each side), walking lunges (6–8 each leg), high knees (20–30 sec), butt kicks (20–30 sec).
- Gentle breathing focus: inhale through nose, exhale through mouth, controlled cadence to limit sudden bronchospasm.
- If advised, use SABA 10–15 min before starting warm-up.

Cool-down template (5–10 min)
- 3–5 min easy walk reducing heart rate.
- Light static stretches: calves, quads, hamstrings, glutes, hip flexors—20–30 sec each.
- Controlled breathing exercises to recover.

Strength sessions (2×/week, 15–20 min) — perform on non-consecutive days
- Bodyweight squat or goblet squat: 2 sets × 8–12 reps
- Single-leg Romanian deadlift (bodyweight or light DB): 2 × 8 each leg
- Glute bridge or single-leg bridge: 2 × 10–12
- Plank: 2 × 20–40 sec
- Side plank: 1–2 × 20–30 sec each side
- Calf raises: 2 × 12–15
Progress load by adding reps, time, or light weight as weeks progress.

12-week plan (3 run sessions per week). Each session lists warm-up, main set, cool-down. If a session would be outdoors in cold, swap for treadmill or move session time to warmer part of day.

Weeks 1–4: Establish baseline, walk–run intervals, build aerobic tolerance
Week 1 (3 sessions)
- Goal: get comfortable moving for 20–30 min.
Session A, B, C:
- Warm-up 8–10 min (as above). Use SABA pre-warm-up if your GP recommends.
- Main: 1 min jog + 1.5 min walk — repeat 8 times (total main ~20 min). Pace: easy conversational pace.
- Cool-down 5–8 min.
Strength: two 15-min sessions on non-run days.

Week 2
Session A:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 1.5 min jog + 2 min walk — repeat 7 times (approx 24.5 min)
Session B:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 90 sec jog + 90 sec walk — repeat 8 times (24 min)
Session C:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 2 min jog + 2.5 min walk — repeat 6 times (27 min)
Cool-down each session.
Strength: two sessions.

Week 3
Session A:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 3 min jog + 2 min walk — repeat 6 times (30 min)
Session B:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 4 min jog + 2 min walk — repeat 4 times (24 min)
Session C:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 5 min jog + 3 min walk — repeat 3 times (24 min)
Cool-down.
Strength as before.

Week 4 (step-back week — slightly easier to consolidate)
Session A:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 4 min jog + 2 min walk — repeat 4 times (24 min)
Session B:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 6 min jog + 3 min walk — repeat 2 times (18 min) + easy 6–8 min jog/walk
Session C:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 20 min continuous easy jog (if comfortable; otherwise 3×6 min jog with 2-min walks)
Cool-down.
Strength: two sessions.

Weeks 5–8: Increase continuous running and total weekly time
Week 5
Session A:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 8 min jog + 3 min walk — repeat 2 times (22 min)
Session B:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 12 min jog + 3 min walk + 8 min jog (total 23 min run time)
Session C:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 20–22 min continuous easy jog (aim for time on feet, not pace)
Cool-down.
Strength: 2 sessions — increase plank times, progress load.

Week 6
Session A:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 10 min jog + 2 min walk + 10 min jog (22 min)
Session B:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 15 min jog + 3 min walk + 8 min jog (23 min)
Session C:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 25 min continuous easy jog (if breathing and symptoms controlled)
Cool-down.
Strength: 2 sessions.

Week 7
Session A:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 20 min continuous jog
Session B:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 12 min easy jog + 3 min walk + 12 min easy jog (27 min)
Session C:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 28–30 min continuous easy jog (aim ~3–4 km depending on pace)
Cool-down.
Strength: 2 sessions.

Week 8 (consolidation + optional easy tempo intro)
Session A:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 25 min continuous jog at easy pace
Session B:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 5 min easy jog, 2 × (6 min steady "comfortably hard" effort with 2 min easy jog between) — keep the faster efforts only if asthma controlled and outdoors conditions are mild; otherwise do steady runs.
Session C:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 30 min continuous easy jog
Cool-down.
Strength: 2 sessions.

Weeks 9–12: Move toward continuous 5K, race prep, taper
Week 9
Session A:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 30 min continuous jog (target ~3–4 km+ depending on pace)
Session B:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 10 min easy jog + 2 × (8 min steady run with 2 min walk/jog between)
Session C:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 35 min continuous easy run (aim to cover near or over 5K if pace allows)
Cool-down.
Strength: 2 sessions.

Week 10
Session A:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 35 min continuous easy run or aim for 4–4.5 km continuous at easy pace
Session B:
- Warm-up.
- Main: Run 20 min continuous at steady comfortable pace (slightly faster than easy but controlled breathing)
Session C:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 40 min continuous easy run OR a paced 5K attempt at easy/moderate intensity (only if asthma stable) — treat this as a trial longer run.
Cool-down.
Strength: 2 sessions.

Week 11 (race-specific practice)
Session A:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 25–30 min easy run with 3 × 2 min slightly faster surges (not sprints) with full recovery — practice inhaler use and breathing control if needed.
Session B:
- Warm-up thoroughly.
- Main: 20–25 min continuous steady run—simulate race pace for short segments (e.g., 3 × 5 min at goal race pace with 2 min easy between).
Session C:
- Warm-up.
- Main: 5K time trial at comfortable effort (aim to complete rather than all-out). If doing outdoors in cold, pick warmest part of day or use indoor treadmill.
Cool-down.
Strength: 1–2 light sessions (reduce load this week).

Week 12 (taper & final race week)
Session A (early in week, 3–4 days before target 5K)
- Warm-up.
- Main: 20 min easy run with 3 × 1 min slightly quicker efforts.
Session B (2 days before race)
- Warm-up.
- Main: 15–20 min easy run; 4 × 30 sec pickups at race effort with full recovery.
Session C (race day)
- Warm-up: extended 10–12 min dynamic warm-up + 2–3 short strides (20–30 sec) if desired. Use SABA 10–15 min before warm-up if your asthma plan recommends it.
- Main: 5K run — aim to maintain steady pace you can sustain. Walk any necessary parts; finishing is the priority.
- Cool-down: 8–10 min walk + stretch and drink fluids.

Pacing guidance
- Early weeks: conversational pace (you can speak in full sentences).
- “Comfortably hard” efforts should allow short sentences only; avoid maximal sprints that can provoke EIA.
- Focus on time/distance goals, not speed. Build confidence and breathing control.

Asthma-specific training notes
- Pre-exercise SABA: follow GP/asthma action plan. Typical timing is 10–15 minutes before starting warm-up, but follow individual prescription.
- Keep inhaler accessible and notify training partners about your asthma and inhaler location.
- Learn your triggers (cold air, pollen, pollution). Use indoor treadmill sessions or adjust timing on high-pollen or poor-air-quality days.
- Breathing techniques: nasal breathing during easy efforts may help warm/humidify air; use diaphragmatic breathing drills outside of runs to improve breath control.
- If you have frequent symptoms during training, re-check with GP or asthma specialist — may need controller therapy review.

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Eat a balanced meal 1.5–3 hours before runs; small snack 30–60 min before if needed (banana, toast).
- Post-run recovery snack: ~20–30 g protein + carbs within 60–90 min (yogurt + fruit, smoothie with protein, sandwich).
- Hydration: drink water regularly; sip before, during (if hot/long sessions), and after.
- Rest: at least one full rest day per week; listen to fatigue cues and reduce volume if very tired or having bronchospasm symptoms.

When to slow down or stop the plan
- Increase in frequency/severity of asthma symptoms despite SABA.
- Need for SABA more than usual despite pre-treatment.
- Chest pain, fainting, or severe shortness of breath.
- New or worsening medical issues — consult GP.

Progress tracking and adjustments
- Keep a simple log: date, session (A/B/C), total time, distance (if using GPS), symptoms (0–3) and inhaler use.
- If you miss multiple sessions, repeat the previous successful week before moving forward.
- If asthma symptoms limit sessions, reduce run intervals or substitute low-impact cardio (cycling, brisk walking, pool) until stable.

Summary
- Three run sessions per week, gradual build from run/walk intervals to continuous 5K.
- Warm-up, pre-treatment with SABA as advised, avoid cold-air high-intensity bursts, indoor alternatives as needed.
- Two short strength sessions weekly, recovery focus, and a cautious taper in week 12.
- Prioritize safety: stop and use inhaler for wheeze, and seek help if symptoms don't respond.

If you want, I can:
- Convert this into a printable week-by-week sheet for the client.
- Provide a sample daily log template.
- Adjust the plan for specific start fitness (if he can already jog a continuous 10–15 min), or for an exact race date.
